answer: Standing is inherited through relics cut from a harbor wall the network surveyed once, so a relic cannot be copied. A claimant must show its relic; accounts backed by the same relic collapse into a single identity, so n aliases never raise weight above one. To climb to the summit tier an operator needs two relics of comparable age, and the k-th relic a surveyor issues costs k squared in escrow, so running n identities costs about n cubed over three. Relics carry their surveyor's seal and cannot be sold or lent: standing is earned, never passed around.
